metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Circuit breaker: if more than half of PRs merged in a 6-week window are LLM-created, new LLM-created PRs are disallowed until back below 50%, with a 10-day minimum cooldown.
domains.accountability_wording: Your contributions are your responsibility; you cannot place any blame on an LLM.

evidence.quote: Comments that are originally created by an LLM posted from a personal user account.
All uses under "⚠️ Allowed with caveats" **must** disclose that an LLM was used.
Your contributions are your responsibility; you cannot place any blame on an LLM.
If more than half of PRs merged in a 6-week window are LLM-created, we disallow merging new LLM-created PRs until we go back below 50%

domains.reasoning: The policy is highly specific about code contributions: it bans LLM-originated comments/issue text/PR descriptions, requires disclosure for trivial changes and machine-translation, sets a detailed pre-arranged/non-critical/well-tested/well-reviewed experiment framework with a 50% circuit-breaker volume cap, and explicitly assigns responsibility for contributions to the contributor. Supervision varies by sub-case (banned, disclosure_required, human_in_the_loop for the experiment) but disclosure is the consistent gating condition across all allowed uses.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of meeting recording/notetaker bots at all
domains.reasoning: The document discusses 'voice/video content originally created or scripted by an LLM' as banned, but this refers to LLM-scripted spoken content posted by a user, not to notetaker/meeting-transcription bots recording discussions. No mention of recorded meetings, transcripts, or closed/small-group content is present.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to non-trivial source comments, doc-comments, safety comments, multi-paragraph comments, and compiler diagnostics; excludes 'trivial' changes and out-of-scope material like the style guide and lang documentation.
domains.accountability_wording: Your contributions are your responsibility; you cannot place any blame on an LLM.

evidence.quote: Documentation that is originally created by an LLM.
This includes non-trivial source comments, such as doc-comments, safety comments, or multiple paragraphs of non-doc-comments.
Your contributions are your responsibility; you cannot place any blame on an LLM.

domains.reasoning: Documentation (a content type per the domain definition) is explicitly banned from being LLM-originated, with a carve-out for trivial changes and disclosure requirements matching the code contributions rules. The general responsibility clause applies to all contributions including docs, giving an accountability holder. Blogs and design assets are not separately named, but documentation is addressed with a clear rule and holder.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on AI use in moderation actions themselves; no supervision level or holder
domains.reasoning: The document is titled a 'moderation policy' and describes penalties, reporting, and moderator discretion for violations of the LLM-usage rules, but this is a policy governing how contributors use LLMs, not a rule about whether/how moderators themselves may use AI to take moderation actions (e.g., auto-flagging, auto-banning). No such provision appears.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Review bots require one-time maintainer approval; must use a separate, clearly-marked, blockable GitHub account; LLM comments must be non-blocking and require explicit reviewer endorsement.
domains.accountability_wording: They are responsible for their own analysis of the LLM's comment and cannot treat it as a CI failure.

evidence.quote: Treating an LLM review as a sufficient condition to merge or reject a change. LLM reviews, if enabled, **must** be advisory-only.
Review bots that post without being approved by a maintainer will be banned.
reviewers must explicitly endorse an LLM comment before blocking a PR. They are responsible for their own analysis of the LLM's comment and cannot treat it as a CI failure.

domains.reasoning: Review is one of the most specifically addressed domains: LLM reviews and 'review bots' are allowed with caveats requiring disclosure, mandatory maintainer approval of the bot account, non-blocking advisory-only comments, and explicit reviewer endorsement/responsibility before any comment can block a PR, plus a requirement that self-review by the author is never substituted.

domains.suggested_improvement: no rule on autonomous/agentic action independent of a human author
domains.reasoning: The 'Experiment: LLM-created code changes' framework always requires a pre-arranged human reviewer, human disclosure, and author/reviewer understanding of the code -- it is human-in-the-loop code contribution, not a rule about an AI agent acting autonomously on the repository (e.g. opening/merging PRs unsupervised). The clause banning processes 'written such that an LLM is required to execute them' concerns documentation authored for humans, not agent autonomy, and does not set a supervision level for autonomous agent action.

domains.rationale_only_mention: many others feel that its negative impact on society and the climate are severe enough that no use is acceptable
domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level or rule on energy/water/carbon impact
domains.reasoning: Climate impact is cited only as a reason some community members reject all LLM use; it is offered as context for the lack of consensus motivating the policy, not as a rule setting any supervision level, scope limit, or accountability holder for environmental impact.

domains.suggested_improvement: no mention of server load or hardware cost/financing
domains.reasoning: No text in this file addresses infrastructure strain (server load, hardware cost or financing) in any capacity, either as rule or rationale.

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on whether project content/data may train models
domains.reasoning: The policy discusses copyright/originality concerns about LLM output reproducing others' training data (e.g. references to 'threshold of originality' and the Google v. Oracle ruling) as background for the 'trivial changes' rule, but never addresses whether this project's own issues, discussions, code, or user data may be used to train models.

unscoped_statements.quote: It's fine to use LLMs to answer questions, analyze, distill, refine, check, suggest, review. But not to **create**.
LLMs work best when used as a tool to write *better*, not *faster*.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The policy is granular and enforceable for code contributions, documentation/comments, and AI-assisted review (naming supervision levels, scope limits, and accountability holders for each), while remaining entirely silent -- neither rule nor rationale -- on notetaker/meeting bots, AI use in moderation actions, autonomous/agentic repository action, infrastructure strain, and the project's own data being used for training; environmental impact appears only as an unresolved community concern cited as background, not as a rule.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
